answer: One concrete defense is to make each agent's reputation costly to build and easy to lose: a new identity starts with near-zero trust, like shale that only becomes solid ground after many layers of verifiable work accumulate. Every transaction leaves a public echo, so peers can audit the record and spot clusters of fresh identities acting in lockstep. Add a small stake, marked saffron in the ledger so anyone can see it, that is slashed on proven abuse; sybils then pay a real cost per identity while honest agents keep earning.
